newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Quantity keeps tea prices down at Colombo auction.
newsitem.headline: Quantity keeps tea prices down at Colombo auction.

text.p: Tea prices at the Colombo auction were marginally lower on Wednesday due to large quantities of coming into the market, brokers said.
"There was demand and orders were coming. But buyers seem to be having trouble absorbing such large quantities," said Rohan Iddawela of brokers Forbes and Walker.
A total of 6.3 million kilograms were on offer, 3.2 million of them low-growns, popular with Middle East and Russian buyers.

"We had a lot of uncatalogued teas in the warehouses because of shortened sales due to holidays in December and January. Those teas are now coming into the market, boosting quantities," Iddawela said.
The next auction, to be held on March 4-5, is expected to have six million kg, brokers said.

On Wednesday, most low-growns fetched lower prices with all grades dropping between one and six rupees. High-grown BOPs were two to four rupees dearer while other grades gained two to three rupees, brokers said.
The anticipated gross auction average was 104 rupees ($1.81) compared to 103.94 last week, they said.
